findings.issue: TypeScript 7.0 (Go-native compiler) has been stable for under five months and ships no stable programmatic API until 7.1, so tooling that embeds the compiler (e.g. typescript-eslint) wouldn't work against it.
findings.suggestion: Fine as-is since the app only invokes tsc via CLI; if editor linting or programmatic transforms are added later, verify ecosystem support first (the package-lock.json already pins the exact version).

summary: The app is maximally conservative: zero experimental, preview, RC or canary APIs, no bundler/compiler flags, and only long-stable DOM/Node/ES2023 features. The sole recency is pinning the current stable majors — Vite 8 (Rolldown, stable 2026-03-12) and TypeScript 7 (native compiler, stable 2026-07-08) — used in completely vanilla, no-config fashion. Risk of breaking-change exposure is minimal and confined to two devDependencies.
